repositories.description: Bitcoin calculator that converts BTC to USD at live CoinGecko prices, then re-prices the same holding across built-in targets from $50K to $1M — plus the pinned 2025 ATH and any target you add — and shows the market cap each target would imply. paragraphs: A real-time Bitcoin calculator webapp that converts BTC to USD at live market prices and projects future portfolio values across price targets.
Live site: calculat-bur.netlify.app — part of the Observation Deck.

The projections are arithmetic, not forecasts: each row is your BTC amount multiplied by that price target. The in-page "How this works" panel explains what the estimated market cap assumes, where the 2025 ATH figure comes from, which chart is real market data and which is arithmetic, and that custom targets are stored only in your browser.
features: Live BTC Price Ticker — Current BTC/USD from CoinGecko with 24h change %, auto-refreshing every 60 seconds, pausing while the tab is backgrounded. A price change counts up to its new value and tints the ticker green or…

BTC/USD Converter — Bidirectional, instant, satoshi-level precision. Enter the holding in BTC, mBTC or sats via a unit switch, or start from a dollar amount. Inputs accept 1,000 and $1,000 as readily as 1000, and…
Quick amounts — One-tap presets appropriate to the selected unit

Price History Chart — Real BTC market data over 24H / 7D / 30D / 90D / 1Y / 5Y / 10Y, with the range's open, close and percentage change stated in text beneath it. Ranges up to a year come from CoinGecko's marketchart;…

Future Value Projections — A horizontal bar ladder and a sortable table showing holdings value at price targets ($50K–$1M), each with gain/loss vs the current price and the Bitcoin market cap that target would imply.…

whatItDoes.text: A real-time Bitcoin calculator webapp that converts BTC to USD at live market prices and projects future portfolio values across price targets.

paragraphs: Comments for static sites — without the comment SaaS.
StaticLayer is a source-available, Cloudflare-native comment system designed for static websites. Your Worker. Your database. No centralized comment platform.
🌐 Website · Try the interactive demo · Docs · Security · Install guide · GitHub
features: 🪙 Proof-of-Work anti-spam — visitors solve a tiny client-side puzzle; no CAPTCHA, no forms of friction.

🛡️ Anti-replay by design — a solved challenge can never be reused, even under concurrent races (proven by tests).
🧑‍💼 Moderation queue — new comments are pending until an admin approves them.
🔒 XSS-safe — comments are plain text only (no Markdown, no HTML). Rendered exclusively with textContent.

repositories.name: leash
repositories.description: Agent wallet with onchain spending policy, built on AUSD and the x402 payment protocol

paragraphs: Leash is a spending allowance for AI agents that they can split among sub-agents, with the rules enforced onchain at every payment.

AUSD supports the ERC-3009 transferWithAuthorization overload that takes a bytes signature and falls back to ERC-1271 when the signer is a contract. This lets the wallet itself be the from address and authorize each transfer through its own logic. The overload selector is 0xcf092995. Live testnet checks confirmed the overload and the fallback path on Base Sepolia AUSD.

repositories.name: ksml

paragraphs: KSML is a wrapper language and interpreter around Kafka Streams that lets you express any topology in a YAML syntax. Simply define your topology as a processing pipeline with a series of steps that your data passes through. Your custom functions can be expressed inline in Python. KSML will read your definition and construct the topology dynamically via the Kafka Streams DSL and run it in GraalVM.
KSML was started by Axual in early 2021 and open-sourced in May 2021.
Kafka Streams is powerful but Java-centric. KSML eliminates the Java boiler-plate through:
features: Declarative YAML for topology wiring
User-defined functions in Python for customized business logic
One command to package and run (container image or in your own JVM)

repositories.name: Bitcoin-PIR
repositories.description: Implementing PIR for Bitcoin UTXO set

paragraphs: Query the Bitcoin UTXO set without revealing which addresses you're interested in.

Today's light wallets leak every address you own to their server, enabling full surveillance of your balances, transactions, and spending habits. Bitcoin PIR uses Private Information Retrieval — a family of cryptographic protocols where the server(s) provably learn nothing about which records you look up — to give light wallets the same privacy as a full node, without the storage cost.
features: Each UTXO lookup can be paired with a Merkle proof query that checks the result against the database's Merkle root. Verification is batched across all addresses in a wallet sync — one proof round covers the whole batch.…

Trust-model note on Merkle verification. Clients check each result's Merkle proof and report the verdict per result (merkleVerified); the caller decides what to do with an unverified one. A client can also verify the…

Wallet sync typically touches dozens of addresses at once. Bitcoin PIR packs multiple addresses into a single PIR round using probabilistic batch codes, so syncing a wallet with 50 addresses takes roughly the same time…

The server hosts the complete Bitcoin UTXO set (815K active script types at time of writing), filtered to exclude dust and very heavy addresses. Light wallets see the same data a full node would return.

Anyone can run a node serving the published database generation (docs/OPERATORGUIDE.md). Free queries are open; a provider chooses per backend what is free, paid, or free while the server has room, and paid queries…

whatItDoes.text: Query the Bitcoin UTXO set without revealing which addresses you're interested in.

repositories.name: halberd
repositories.description: A security guard for AI assistants. It checks every tool an AI tries to use, preventing data leaks and unauthorized commands.

paragraphs: Useful access, with limits you choose. Halberd checks an AI assistant's tool requests against your policies before letting them through.
You ask an AI assistant to look up ten student records. So far, so useful. But the same database tool can receive a command to erase an entire table. Who checks which request gets through?

Halberd sits between the assistant and its connected tools. You choose the rules: which tools are permitted, which commands are forbidden, and which sensitive values should be removed from responses. Halberd applies those rules as requests and responses pass through it.

repositories.name: chatgpt-subtitle-translator
repositories.description: Token efficient translation tool based on ChatGPT or any OpenAI compatible LLM chat completion API

paragraphs: Large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, have demonstrated their capabilities as a robust translator, capable of handling common natural languages with contextual understanding, as well as unconventional forms of writing like word scrambling. However, it may not always produce a deterministic output or adhere to line-to-line correlation, potentially disrupting the timing of subtitles, even when instructed to follow precise instructions and with the model temperature parameter set to 0.

This utility uses the OpenAI ChatGPT API to translate text, with a specific focus on line-based translation, especially for SRT subtitles. The translator optimizes token usage by removing SRT overhead and grouping text into batches, resulting in arbitrary length translations without excessive token consumption while ensuring a one-to-one match between line input and output.
features: Web User Interface (Web UI) and Command Line Interface (CLI)
Supports Structured Output: for more concise results, enabled by default in the Web UI and CLI

Supports Prompt Caching: by including the full context of translated data, the system instruction and translation context are packaged to work well with prompt caching, controlled with -c, --context (CLI only)
Supports any OpenAI API compatible providers such as running Ollama locally
Line-based batching: avoids token limit per request, reduces overhead token wastage, and maintains translation context to a certain extent

repositories.name: potemkin-pipeline
repositories.description: Offline single-file screensaver/PWA that simulates an AI coding agent at work — fake terminal, fake dashboards, zero real code, all theater, zero dependencies.

paragraphs: A fake AI coding agent screensaver. Offline, single-file, installable PWA — zero dependencies, zero real code, 100% convincing from across the room.

An offline, single-file browser app that simulates the theater of an autonomous AI coding agent at work — streaming tool calls, second-guessing itself, fixing bugs it invented moments earlier, shipping to prod, and surviving the occasional boss-level drama (a runaway process on a critical box, a flailing CI pipeline, a flame graph, a btop meltdown, a volumetric DDoS). Think hacker-typer, but for vibe-coding an AI agent instead of hammering a keyboard.

It does not write any code. It performs the idea of writing code — the way a community-theater actor performs the idea of brain surgery. Every counter, graph, and "172× faster" is a confident lie computed by a seeded PRNG. It's a Potemkin village for your terminal: real-looking and convincing to a non-technical observer from across the room, but it will not survive anyone who actually reads it (nor is it trying to).

whatItDoes.text: A fake AI coding agent screensaver. Offline, single-file, installable PWA — zero dependencies, zero real code, 100% convincing from across the room.

paragraphs: One intuitive modelling interface. Three ways to solve.

DynaPlex is an optimization library for formulating and solving Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), i.e. for identifying well-performing policies that select actions based on complete or partial observations of the state. Its design enables clean modelling and efficient solving of problems arising in operations management (OM) and related fields: supply chain management, transportation, manufacturing, warehousing, maintenance and process optimization.

You write a model once, in DynaML: a purpose-built modelling language whose syntax is canonical Python, extended with modelling primitives such as discrete distributions. Models execute on a multi-threaded engine with a bundled LLVM JIT, so you read and write plain Python and get auto-vectorized C++ speed. That one model then feeds every method in the library:

repositories.name: Esure
repositories.description: Open-source Stellar Testnet scenario runner and dashboard for validating XLM and issued-asset payment flows with structured, sanitized reports.

paragraphs: Esure is an open-source testing and simulation toolkit that helps developers validate Stellar payment flows before integrating them into production applications. It turns multi-step Testnet operations into repeatable scenarios with structured reports, transaction links, balance changes, and readable failure explanations.
Esure is an MVP built exclusively for Stellar Testnet. It must not be used for Mainnet transactions or real-value assets.

A realistic Stellar payment test spans account creation, Friendbot funding, trustline configuration, transaction submission, ledger confirmation, and balance verification. Rebuilding that flow manually makes failures difficult to reproduce and easy to misdiagnose. Esure packages the full process into versioned scenarios that can be executed repeatedly and inspected through one consistent report format.
features: 13 Bundled Scenarios: XLM payments, issued assets, trustlines, expected failures, multi-op transactions (Testnet only)
Developer-Friendly Errors: Plain-English explanations for 30+ Stellar error codes with causes and fix suggestions
Command-Line Interface: Run scenarios from terminal or CI pipelines (run from source; not yet published to npm)
Declarative Testing: Bounded JSON/YAML scenario definitions with schema validation
Isolated Execution: Fresh Testnet accounts per run, no cross-run contamination

whatItDoes.text: Esure is an open-source testing and simulation toolkit that helps developers validate Stellar payment flows before integrating them into production applications. It turns multi-step Testnet operations into repeatable scenarios with structured reports, transaction links, balance changes, and readable failure explanations.

repositories.name: freeboard
repositories.description: A damn-sexy, open source real-time dashboard builder for IOT and other web mashups. A free open-source alternative to Geckoboard.

paragraphs: Freeboard is a turn-key HTML-based "engine" for dashboards. Besides a nice looking layout engine, it provides a plugin architecture for creating datasources (which fetch data) and widgets (which display data)— freeboard then does all the work to connect the two together. Another feature of freeboard is its ability to run entirely in the browser as a single-page static web app without the need for a server. The feature makes it extremely attractive as a front-end for embedded devices which may have limited ability to serve complex and dynamic web pages.

The code here is the client-side portion of what you see when you visit a freeboard at It does not include any of the server-side code for user management, saving to a database or public/private functionality— this is left up to you to implement should you want to use freeboard as an online service.
features: the distance between the waterline and the main deck or weather deck of a ship or between the level of the water and the upper edge of the side of a small boat.
the act of freeing data from below the "waterline" and exposing it to the world.
a damn-sexy, open source real-time dashboard builder/viewer for IOT and other web mashups.

paragraphs: Neuromorphic Computing Engine. SNN AI Architecture base from biology.

A living brain for embodied AI. Learns in seconds. Runs everywhere - from ESP32 microcontrollers to GPU clusters. Axicor is a Spiking Neural Network engine designed for biological realism and absolute determinism. No backpropagation. No static computation graphs. Neurons fire spikes, axons physically grow through 3D space, weak synapses are pruned, strong ones fortified - all in real-time, without halting the simulation.
Watch the live demo -> - an ant agent in Gymnasium-AntV4, no pre-training, walking within 30 seconds of spawn.
features: Behavior out of the box. An ant agent spawned in Gymnasium-AntV4 stands upright within seconds and begins exploratory locomotion within 30 seconds of instantiation - with zero pre-training. No gradient descent, no…

Bit-exact determinism across hardware. Integer-only physics (GLIF, GSOP) guarantees identical simulation results on an RTX 4090, AMD RDNA, or an ESP32. No floating-point drift, no cross-platform divergence.

Real-time structural plasticity. Axons physically grow and prune during the Night Phase while the Day Phase hot-loop keeps ticking. No "training mode" vs "inference mode" divide - the brain rewires itself while it lives.
Modest hardware friendly. Reference demos run on a GTX 1080 Ti. No cloud-scale compute required.

paragraphs: clever-f.vim extends f, F, t and T mappings for more convenience. Instead of ;, f is available to repeat after you type f{char} or F{char}. F after f{char} and F{char} is also available to undo a jump. t{char} and T{char} are ditto. This extension makes a repeat easier and makes you forget the existence of ;. You can use ; for other key mapping. In addition, this extension provides many convenient features like target character highlighting, smart case matching and so on.
If you want to reset the searching character without moving cursor, map (clever-f-reset) to your favorite key.
Lastly, you can customize the behavior of the mappings and features.
features: clever-f.vim can highlight the characters in the line which can be directly jumped to. With this feature, you can easily understand where cursor can move by the f{char} input before inputting {char}.

For example, when 'aba' is in the current line, cursor can reach the first 'a' with fa but cannot reach the second 'a'. In this case, the first 'a' is highlighted but the second 'a' is not when typing f.
To enable this feature, set 1 to g:cleverfmarkdirect in your vimrc. Note that setting 1 after Vim starts does not work.

You can specify the timeout for repeating the previous target character on f, F, t and T mappings. If the interval of these mappings is greater than the one you specified, clever-f.vim resets its state to make you input…
When target character highlighting is enabled, the highlight can be cleared after specific timeout.

repositories.name: inFairness
repositories.description: PyTorch package to train and audit ML models for Individual Fairness

paragraphs: Intuitively, an individually fair Machine Learning (ML) model treats similar inputs similarly. Formally, the leading notion of individual fairness is metric fairness (Dwork et al., 2011); it requires:
$$ dy (h(x1), h(x2)) \leq L dx(x1, x2) \quad \forall \quad x1, x2 \in X $$

Here, $h: X \rightarrow Y$ is a ML model, where $X$ and $Y$ are input and output spaces; $dx$ and $dy$ are metrics on the input and output spaces, and $L \geq 0$ is a Lipchitz constant. This constrained optimization equation states that the distance between the model predictions for inputs $x1$ and $x2$ is upper-bounded by the fair distance between the inputs $x1$ and $x2$. Here, the fair metric $dx$ encodes our intuition of which samples should be treated similarly by the ML model, and in designing so, we ensure that for input samples considered similar by the fair metric $dx$, the model…

paragraphs: Sham‑Wah is a web application currently being developed as part of the IntForOut Project. Designed as a companion to OutdoorPressure knowledge graph, it enables non‑experts to query and explore the graph through a user-friendly interface, allowing users to search and discover the wide range of resources (scientific papers, datasets, scripts, services, etc...) produced and used by the project’s research teams.

I wanted a short, pleasant‑sounding name for a Knowledge Graph Query Framework, ideally with a nod to knowledge graph, querying and alpine ecology. Since the project focuses on wildlife disturbance in mountain environments, I explored animal‑themed names and naturally thought of the chamois, an animal I love.

While searching for inspiration, I found an English forum discussing how to pronounce chamois. Someone wrote it as “sham‑wah”, and it immediately clicked: unique spelling, easy to pronounce, and a subtle reference to the real animal. During my research I discovered that chamois is also an HTML color name, which inspired the color theme used in the app.

repositories.name: rwa-token-project
repositories.description: Verified Sepolia RWA token demo with O(1) ETH dividend accounting, 14 Solidity tests, and a live Next.js dashboard.

paragraphs: PropertyToken is an evidence-first Sepolia engineering demo for distributing ETH yield to ERC-20 holders without iterating over the holder set. It combines a fixed-supply Solidity contract, O(1) magnified dividend accounting, transfer-side entitlement corrections, a Hardhat verification pipeline, and a public Next.js dashboard.

Problem. A naive dividend distributor loops over every holder, making deposits progressively more expensive and eventually impractical. It also risks assigning past yield to wallets that buy tokens only after a distribution.

Contribution. The dividend core adapts the established magnified-dividend and signed-correction pattern used by Roger Wu's ERC-1726 reference implementation, which in turn credits PoWH3D as earlier prior art. My work focuses on the Solidity 0.8/OpenZeppelin 5 architecture, carry-forward remainder accounting, permission and pause boundaries, transfer and claim edge cases, oracle and valuation integration, testing, deployment, exact-match verification, and evidence-oriented documentation—not invention of the underlying dividend-per-share algorithm.

paragraphs: The trace layer under a quality-management system. qmstrace keeps the state, traceability and audit evidence of a software project's work products, so that an auditor's questions are answered by query instead of by assembly. ISO/IEC 29110 is the first standard it knows; the standard is data, not code.

It is a command-line tool installed into repositories that already exist. It holds no project data and owns no evidence: it reads markers where people and coding agents already write — a requirement's heading, a line under a design section, a tag on a test — judges them, and points at evidence that stays in its home system.

Status. Setup, trace queries, coverage checks, the project-wide check run in the ledger, baseline and change guards, suspects and the offline browser work locally, for Python (pytest) and C# (xUnit) repos, with JUnit and TRX results. Pinned imports and signatures are not built yet. See the tracker.

Hardware-agnostic neural network inference + training for .NET — C# compute kernels that run on WebGPU, CUDA, OpenCL, WebGL, Wasm, and CPU via SpawnDev.ILGPU.

SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML implements neural network inference AND training as native GPU compute kernels written entirely in C#. Models run as compute shaders transpiled from C# — no ONNX Runtime, no JavaScript, no native binaries. The same code runs in the browser (Blazor WebAssembly) and on desktop. Drop in a model file — ONNX, TFLite, GGUF, or any of 7 inference formats — and run it on any of six backends. Train custom models directly on your GPU in the browser — no server, no Python, no CUDA install.
features: What actually works: Docs/DEMOANDMODELSTATUS.md is the source of truth — a per-demo VERIFIED / PARTIAL / WIP table with the test that proves each one. We mark stubs as WIP honestly, so a demo never lies to you.

Demos - 15 VERIFIED end-to-end (most matched numerically against ONNX Runtime: classification, style, depth, detection, pose, face, CLIP, background-removal, super-res, text-gen, embeddings, sentiment, inspector,…

16 inference pipelines — Classification, StyleTransfer, SuperResolution, DepthEstimation, ObjectDetection, PoseEstimation, FaceDetection, TextClassification, ZeroShotClassification (CLIP), BackgroundRemoval,…

GPU training engine — Draw custom gestures, train a CNN classifier in real-time on your GPU, test instantly. Softmax-CE MLP training powers System One heads. Backpropagation, gradient descent, Adam optimizer — all in C#…

repositories.name: DigitVision
repositories.description: Handwritten digit recognition with a CNN trained on MNIST (99.32% accuracy). Upload or snap a photo and get the predicted digit with confidence and full preprocessing visualization. Built with TensorFlow, OpenCV, and Streamlit.

paragraphs: Handwritten digit recognition, powered by deep learning.
Upload a photo or snap one with your camera, and a CNN trained on MNIST tells you which digit it sees, with a confidence score and a full look at how the image was processed.

MNIST models usually stop at a notebook: great accuracy on clean 28×28 test images, and no idea what happens with a real photo. DigitVision closes that gap. It pairs a compact, regularized CNN with a computer-vision preprocessing pipeline that turns messy, real-world photos of handwritten digits into MNIST-style input, and wraps everything in a clean Streamlit web app.
features: Two input modes: upload an image (PNG/JPG) or take a photo directly with your camera.
Smart digit extraction: detects red ink via HSV color masking, with an automatic Otsu-threshold fallback for dark pen on light paper.
MNIST-style normalization: crops, scales to 20 px, pads to 28×28 and centers the digit by its center of mass, the same way MNIST was built.
Transparent results: predicted digit, confidence level (high / medium / low), top-3 predictions and a probability chart for all ten classes.
"How DigitVision saw your image": inspect the detection box, binary mask and the exact 28×28 model input.

whatItDoes.text: Handwritten digit recognition, powered by deep learning.

repositories.name: ORCA
repositories.description: ORCA: Generative Conformal Prediction with Optimized Coverage Allocation (NeurIPS 2026)

paragraphs: Standard CP, PCP and ORCA on the same generated samples. Try the interactive demo.

In this paper, we propose ORCA (Optimized Ranking and Coverage Allocation), a method that turns samples from a generative model into prediction sets with guaranteed coverage. Instead of one radius for every sample, ORCA learns a separate radius for each density rank, which gives compact, disconnected sets that follow the shape of the distribution.
features: Explore. Draw samples from the generative model and rank them by local density, densest first.
Optimize. On an exploration split, learn one radius per rank: the smallest balls that still cover the target share of outcomes.
Calibrate. On a separate calibration split, scale every radius by one common factor, which gives finite-sample marginal coverage.

whatItDoes.text: Standard CP, PCP and ORCA on the same generated samples. Try the interactive demo.

repositories.name: semanticache
repositories.description: Semantic caching layer for LLM APIs: cuts cost and latency by reusing answers for similar prompts using embeddings.

paragraphs: A semantic caching proxy for LLM APIs. It sits in front of any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, recognizes when a new prompt means the same thing as one it already answered — even worded differently — and returns the stored answer instead of paying for another model call. A small set of agents keep that safe and tuned without a human watching a dashboard.
Live demo (client-side simulator, no backend needed): GitHub Pages, docs/index.html Full stack: FastAPI + Redis (exact cache) + Qdrant (semantic cache) + Prometheus + Grafana

A plain vector-similarity cache is dangerous: "Is 15% too much interest?" and "Is 25% too much interest?" embed almost identically, and so do "is this medicine safe" and "is this medicine not safe." Serving the wrong one back with confidence is worse than a cache miss. SemantiCache treats that as the core problem, not an edge case:
features: Deterministic safety guard — numbers and negations must match between
Verifier agent — matches that land just under the similarity threshold
Governor agent — watches how often the guard blocks a should-have-been-fine
Cost-aware router — model: "auto" sends short, simple prompts to a cheap
PII redaction & tenant isolation — emails, card numbers, and phone numbers

paragraphs: EKIP (Educational Knowledge Intelligence Platform) is an evidence-driven, multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platform designed to help students, educators, and researchers learn, practice, research, and explore educational domains.

Unlike standard single-model chatbots that generate unverified text, EKIP coordinates a 12-node LangGraph StateGraph pipeline, a rule-based deterministic knowledge planner, 9 specialized knowledge source agents, a hybrid RAG engine (ChromaDB + BM25 + Cross-Encoder Reranking), and an automated evidence verification layer to deliver structured, grounded learning experiences.

Target Document Resolution: Matches query terms against uploaded workspace documents using stem matching and boundary rules.
Document Usage Modes: Supports REQUIRED, PREFERRED, OPTIONAL, or EXCLUDED document retrieval modes.

repositories.name: SecureVault
repositories.description: End-to-end encrypted file sharing over an untrusted server. AES-256-GCM, X25519, Ed25519, SHA-2 and HKDF implemented from scratch in Python, with a live MITM attacker demo. Applied Cryptography project, Birzeit University.

features: All cryptography on the client. The server only stores and relays opaque bytes.

paragraphs: A transparent app store built around public releases, inspectable metadata, and automation you can actually follow.
Saw a few people asking about "trackers" flagged in App Manager or TrackerControl, so wanted to clear up what those actually are.

Orion Store is an Android-first store client that leans on public sources instead of hiding everything behind a private service layer. The app pulls catalog data from public JSON, resolves releases from GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg, and keeps the delivery path understandable enough that users can see where things come from and how updates are discovered.
features: Scanners flag library components by name, not active surveillance.
Everything flagged comes from one library, the Unity Ads SDK behind the optional "Fuel the Code" quest.

Since 2.4.5 Orion strips everything from it that Fuel the Code does not need: its app-start hook, its background service, and the advertising ID and ad-measurement permissions. What is left is FullScreenWebViewDisplay,…
Unity only starts when you tap to watch a rewarded video in "Fuel the Code" for XP. It never runs at app start.
There are zero background services, no banner ads, and no advertising ID. Orion collects and sends no user data.

repositories.name: Zeus-Protocol
repositories.description: Self-contained personal wellness app — agenda, routines, supplements, tasks, calendar and biomarker tracking, plus Whoop/Apple Health integrations, in a single HTML file with Supabase-backed accounts.

paragraphs: ZEUS Protocol is a personal wellness tracker built as a single self-contained HTML file — no build step, no framework — served from GitHub Pages and added to the iPhone home screen as a web app.

Agenda merges routines, supplement blocks and calendar events into one timeline, with a live eating-window countdown. Routines support optional items you switch on per day, weekday scheduling and streak counters. Supplements are grouped into timed blocks with doses. Tasks track one-off and dated to-dos with overdue tracking, separate from the daily routine. Calendar subscribes to iCal feeds through a Cloudflare Worker proxy, with month, week and day views. Bio reads biomarkers from lab PDFs — including scanned reports with no text layer, via an in-browser OCR fallback (Tesseract.js) — and…

Accounts run on Supabase (hosted in the EU), with local-first sync: the app works fully offline from local storage and syncs on sign-in. A GDPR consent gate, privacy page and account-deletion flow are built in. Biomarker data never leaves the device — it stays in local storage only, whether or not you're signed in. A full JSON export/import covers backup and portability regardless of sign-in state. Each account can personalise which tabs are shown and rename the app to their own "'s Protocol".

whatItDoes.text: ZEUS Protocol is a personal wellness tracker built as a single self-contained HTML file — no build step, no framework — served from GitHub Pages and added to the iPhone home screen as a web app.

repositories.name: ragnapax
repositories.description: Ragnarok point-sharing planner for Tokyo Debunkers

paragraphs: Plan fair point sharing for Ragnarok in Tokyo Debunkers. Tap the towns each of the four guilds in your group starts with, choose a goal, and the planner works out who declares on what each day so every guild ends up with the same reward. One person plans for the group and shares the result as a link (or pastes it into chat); everyone else just opens it.

Ragnarok (officially Game Of Claws: Ragnarok, often just Ragna or Rag) runs from Wednesday to Monday. Every group plays the same map that week, and the game hands out starting towns at random, so each group plans its own week. Starting towns appear early on Wednesday; plan before declares open at 11:00 server time.
Everything runs on the player's phone: there is no server, no account and nothing is uploaded.
features: Tap-to-assign map editor. Pick a guild, tap its towns; the selection
moves to the next guild once one is complete, and any leftover town is Vacant automatically. Used to spreadsheets? An advanced option lists the towns instead, each with its guild to pick.
Two goals. Equal resources, the default (the same number of town-,
dorm- and castle-days for every guild), or equal points (towns, dorms and the castle are worth 1, 2 and 3 points a day, on every map, with the castle and dorms shared out too).
Use every kingdom. Optionally hold as much of the map as possible on

repositories.name: fraud-detection-system
repositories.description: End-to-end fraud detection system built on the 6.36M-row PaySim1 dataset. Compares supervised classification and unsupervised anomaly detection, handles extreme class imbalance with class weighting, SMOTE and ADASYN, uses leakage-safe feature engineering and threshold optimization, and includes SHAP explainability and a Streamlit demo.

paragraphs: Data Science Internship Project — Codec Technologies

A post-transaction fraud-monitoring pipeline built on PaySim1, a 6.36-million-row synthetic mobile-money dataset. An eight-experiment comparison matrix plus a tuned XGBoost (nine candidates in all) — spanning anomaly detection (models fit on normal transactions only) and supervised classification, with three different imbalance-handling strategies — are compared head-to-head on the validation set before one final model is evaluated on the held-out test set.

Headline result: at its validation-chosen operating threshold, the final model (a tuned XGBoost) catches 99.59% of fraud with zero false positives (F1 = 0.9980, AUC-ROC = 0.9992) on 415,562 held-out test transactions.

repositories.name: OpenSurge-for-Mac
repositories.description: Surge-style whole-home gateway and control plane for macOS with IPv4/IPv6 support— mihomo TUN, dnsmasq-powered DHCP/DNS, per-device routing, and an agent-friendly validation workspace.

paragraphs: 把 Mac 变成可按设备分流的 Surge 风格全屋透明代理网关——既可让指定设备通过旁路由手动接入，也支持 DHCP/DNS 自动接管与实验性下游 IPv6 接管

OpenSurge for Mac 是一个开源的 Surge 风格 macOS 网关与控制面。多数用户可以先从 旁路由模式开始：主路由 DHCP 保持开启，只让需要接入的设备使用稳定 IPv4，并把网关和 DNS 指向 Mac。需要让同一局域网的设备自动接入时，也可以选择局域网 DHCP 接管；有独立 AP、SSID 或 VLAN 时，则可以使用独立下游 LAN。三种模式均可按需启用实验性的 IPv6 接管。
无论采用哪种模式，你都可以为已登记设备配置不同的出口策略：手机和 Mac 一起走规则 分流、游戏机连美服、电视走流媒体节点。在局域网 DHCP 接管和独立下游 LAN 模式下， 接入相应网络的手机、电视、PS5 和 VR 设备，都可以自动从 Mac 获取 DHCP/DNS，无需逐台 修改网关和 DNS。
features: 导入已有的 mihomo 配置或订阅是可选能力；默认折叠的全局附加配置可以单独添加节点、
Web GUI 实时展示每台设备的连接、上下行流量和实际出口链；菜单栏随时查看网关状态与恢复提醒。
菜单栏与 Web GUI 提供默认关闭、仅本次运行有效的合盖保持运行开关。

whatItDoes.text: 把 Mac 变成可按设备分流的 Surge 风格全屋透明代理网关——既可让指定设备通过旁路由手动接入，也支持 DHCP/DNS 自动接管与实验性下游 IPv6 接管

repositories.name: regex-parity
repositories.description: The same regex gives different answers in JavaScript, Python and Java on real-world text. regex-parity makes regex rules agree across languages, and proves it. Live demo: https://yauhenbichel.github.io/regex-parity/

paragraphs: The same regular expression can give different answers in JavaScript, Python and Java. It happens as soon as text contains accented letters, look-alike characters, smart quotes or invisible characters, which is most real text.
For example, a rule meant to catch false reassurance, checked against That's definitely harmleſs. (with a long s, U+017F, in "harmless"):

regex-parity is a small library with the same functions in JavaScript, Python, Java, Go, Rust, C# and Ruby. It makes one set of regex rules give the same answer in all of them, and comes with a command that checks your rules before you ship them.

whatItDoes.text: The same regular expression can give different answers in JavaScript, Python and Java. It happens as soon as text contains accented letters, look-alike characters, smart quotes or invisible characters, which is most real text.

repositories.name: astrolabe
repositories.description: A self-hosted, open-source alternative to Obsidian: notes, graph and a built-in blog. Web, desktop and Android.

paragraphs: A self-hosted, open-source alternative to Obsidian, with publishing built in.

Astrolabe is a Markdown notes app that runs on your own server. It opens a folder of plain files, including an existing Obsidian vault, and you reach it from any browser, the desktop app or the Android app. Notes you mark as public become a blog on the same server. Compared with Obsidian:
features: Publishing is built in: publish: true puts a note on your blog, with RSS, reader comments and scheduled posts. No Publish subscription.
No sync service: the server holds the vault, every device opens the same notes, and history is backed up to a git remote you own.
A web app: your notes from any device with a browser, at home or behind your own domain, plus desktop (Linux, Windows) and Android apps.
Your vault as it is: wikilinks, embeds, callouts, properties, highlights and footnotes are read as Obsidian writes them, and the folder keeps working in Obsidian.

Live-preview editor. Markdown renders as you type and the source comes back under the caret; wikilinks with autocomplete, backlinks, embeds, callouts, tables you edit in place, footnotes and vim keys.

whatItDoes.text: A self-hosted, open-source alternative to Obsidian, with publishing built in.

requirements.text: No analytics, no CDN requests, no account.

paragraphs: 10 open-source APIs for healthcare, fitness and wellness products, from Zee Palm Labs.
Deploy to Vercel in one click and add your Claude, OpenAI or Gemini key. Each API lives in one file, so you can change its request and response shape without touching anything else.
The 5 deterministic endpoints need no key and return in milliseconds. The AI endpoints add code-based guardrails on top of the model, so the model can't skip them:
features: front-desk-intake: an emergency (chest pain, stroke signs, suicidal language…) is always escalated, even if the model says "routine" or the provider is down.
meal-plan: daily totals are recalculated in code and every ingredient is checked against the client's allergies.
label-scan: doses are compared against adult tolerable upper limits.
session-notes: the transcript is scanned for crisis language.

repositories.name: LMS-MERN
repositories.description: LMS-MERN: A full-stack Learning Management System with Authentication, Role-based Access, Notes Management, Cloudinary Integration, and Syllabus Uploads.

paragraphs: A full-stack learning management system for RGPV engineering students. It provides unit-wise notes, curated important questions, previous year papers and syllabus PDFs, organised by branch, year and semester, with an integrated study assistant.

Learnify is built around a single shared curriculum. The subject codes, their names and their unit breakdowns live in shared/curriculum.json at the repository root and are read by both the API and the web client, so the two can never disagree about what a subject is called or which year and semester it belongs to.

The API is an Express application backed by MongoDB. Files are stored on Cloudinary. Authentication uses a signed JWT with an email one-time code, an optional Google sign in and a password reset flow. The client is a React single page application that renders the notes, the previous year papers, the important questions, the syllabus, a timetable and two study tools.
features: Registration with an emailed one-time code, and a rate limited, attempt capped verification flow
Sign in with a password, with Google, or with a single use reset link
Student, teacher and administrator roles, enforced on the server rather than only in the interface
Profile editing, including an academic record, social links and custom sections
Notes organised by branch, year, semester, subject and unit, with a PDF preview and a real download counter

paragraphs: El sitio personal : un proyecto Quarto (type: website) en español con blog, repositorio docente (cursos/), publicaciones y páginas de contacto, que además es el hub de una familia de 11 blogs temáticos. Los artículos y entradas usan la extensión apaquarto para salir en HTML, PDF y DOCX con formato APA 7 desde un mismo .qmd. Los 11 blogs son submódulos git en pubs/pub, cada uno con su repo, su quarto.yml y su sitio Netlify; el hub es la fuente de verdad del tema (SCSS, JS, extensiones y filtros Lua, meta/workspace.yml → verdad:) y lo propaga con scripts/sync-theme-pubs.sh.

No es un framework de documentos (eso es escritura), ni el estándar docente (eso es docencia), ni el lugar donde se escribe un post de un blog…

paragraphs: The free IFTTT/Zapier alternative for developers to automate their workflows based on GitHub actions, option to run self-hosted without GitHub as well

Actionsflow helps you automate workflows - it's a free IFTTT/Zapier alternative for developers. With Actionsflow you can connect your favorite apps, data, and APIs, receive notifications of actions as they occur, sync files, collect data, and more. We implemented it based on Github actions, and you use a YAML file to build your workflows. The configuration format is the same as Github actions, which makes it easy for you to get going if you've explored Github actions before. You can also use any Github actions as your job's steps.
You can learn more about the core concepts of Actionsflow here.
features: Totally Free! Actionsflow is based on Github actions. To run an Actionsflow workflow, all you need to do is create a repository from the Actionsflow template repository, or, you can also deploy a self-hosted version.
Leverage Community Triggers. You can use community-provided triggers like Slack, RSS, Webhook, Typeform, Email, Reddit, NPM, Telegram, Twitter, etc. You can also easily create your own triggers.

Support Almost ALL Actions of Github Actions. Actionsflow uses act (a tool for running GitHub Actions locally) to run the jobs on your workflow file. With these awesome Github actions, you can connect with IFTTT,…
Support Self-Hosted You can run Actionsflow based on both GitHub Repository or a self-hosted version.

Simple Workflow Configuration. The Actionsflow configuration format is the same as Github actions. If you've written a Github actions file before, you'll find defining an Actionsflow workflow file really easy.

A WYSIWYG rich-text editor engine, written from scratch. No ProseMirror, Lexical, Slate, Quill or Draft.js code anywhere in it, and no runtime dependencies in any package it ships.

Trevixal is not a finished application. It is the building block you put inside your own (a CMS, a support desk, a notes tool, an internal wiki) so that the people using it get the writing surface they expect from Google Docs or Notion, while your app keeps hold of the document, the storage and the chrome around it.

paragraphs: A grep-like tool which understands source code syntax and allows for manipulation in addition to search.

Like grep, regular expressions are a core primitive. Unlike grep, additional capabilities allow for higher precision, with options for manipulation. This allows srgn to operate along dimensions regular expressions and IDE tooling (Rename all, Find all references, ...) alone cannot, complementing them.

srgn is organized around actions to take (if any), acting only within precise, optionally language grammar-aware scopes. In terms of existing tools, think of it as a mix of tr, sed, ripgrep and tree-sitter, with a design goal of simplicity: if you know regex and the basics of the language you are working with, you are good to go.

repositories.name: hospital-mgmt
repositories.description: Hospital Management System in Python: hash tables, AVL trees, heaps, a B+ tree and graphs implemented from scratch, with a Tkinter desktop app and a Streamlit web demo

paragraphs: Live demo: hospital-mgmt-sys.streamlit.app (web version of the Tkinter app; each visitor gets their own copy of the demo hospital)
A desktop application that runs a hospital's day-to-day records: patients, appointments, staff, pharmacy inventory and billing, plus emergency triage and routing around the building.

The design question was which data structure each module needs so that every common operation stays at O(1) or O(log n) as the number of records grows. Every structure is implemented from scratch in Python.
features: Appointment booking checks a doctor's time slots in an AVL tree to reject double bookings. Only the floor and ceiling neighbours of the requested time can overlap it, so the check is O(log n). When a day is full, a FIFO…

Pharmacy stock uses a min-heap keyed on expiry date, so the earliest-expiring batch is always dispensed first, expired batches are discarded before they can be dispensed, and low stock raises a reorder alert.
Emergency triage uses a max-heap on severity (ties go to the earliest arrival), so the most critical patient is always at the top.
Billing indexes bills in a B+ tree by issue date for fast date-range reports, and ranks overdue bills with a max-heap.
Facility map finds the shortest route between departments with Dijkstra and shows which areas are still reachable (BFS) when some are closed.

paragraphs: trading-mcp is a TypeScript workspace that exposes market and trading capabilities through two clients: an MCP stdio server for AI assistants and a Hono REST API for quotes, screening, and signals. A shared core normalizes types, provider adapters, validation, caching, retries, rate limiting, and the Alpaca trading client.

A safe research loop: ask the MCP server for a quote or technicals, use the screener API to compare symbols, and inspect portfolio state with paper trading enabled. The same shared core keeps the clients consistent.

This is engineering infrastructure and research tooling, not investment advice. Market data can be delayed or unavailable, and order tools can reach a real brokerage account when configured. Keep paper trading enabled until an explicit, separately reviewed safety policy exists.

paragraphs: FlexLight is a real-time path tracer for the web, built with TypeScript. It renders complex, dynamic 3D scenes directly in a browser canvas through WebGPU, with a WebGL 2 backend at feature parity.
features: ReSTIR PT Enhanced: NVIDIA's ReSTIR PT Enhanced (Lin et al., 2026) reuses paths across pixels and frames and converges over 20x faster than plain path tracing (WebGPU).
Path tracing: BSDFs with importance sampling, environment map importance sampling, a two-level BVH and dynamic scenes.
Rasterization: a rasterizer on the WebGL 2 backend.
Assets and lights: .obj models, PBR materials (roughness, metallic, emission), point lights and environment maps.
Post-processing: temporal accumulation, FXAA, TAA and tone mapping.

repositories.name: nkipy
repositories.description: NKIPy: Rapid Prototyping on Trainium

paragraphs: NKIPy is an experimental project that provides a NumPy-like tensor-level programming layer on top of NKI (Neuron Kernel Interface). It enables developers to write kernels for rapid prototyping of their ML programs at good performance, while abstracting away low-level hardware details and tiling strategies from developers.

NKIPy is designed for AWS Trainium and depends on components of the AWS Neuron SDK to function. While NKIPy uses Neuron SDK components, it is not an official part of the Neuron SDK. It requires the Neuron Compiler and Neuron Runtime to compile and execute kernels. NKIPy currently lowers tensor operations to HLO and then calls Neuron Compiler (neuronx-cc) to generate NKI code or executables as outputs.

This project is at a prototype/alpha level and is not intended for customers to use in production deployments. You should expect incomplete features and breaking API changes. There is no guarantee of API stability, ongoing maintenance, or future support at this time. We welcome you to experiment with NKIPy, and we appreciate feedback, bug reports, and contributions via GitHub Issues and Pull Requests.

repositories.name: bemtvi
repositories.description: A fast and extensible vim-style editor

paragraphs: bemtvi (pronounced ben-tee-vee) is a modal, vim-style editor architected from scratch — modal editing, Lua plugins, treesitter highlighting, and LSP, built on a fully async, client-server design.
You may be thinking: why another editor instead of using or improving neovim?

Neovim is amazing. It was my main editor for a while, and bemtvi owes it a lot: the client-server split, Lua as the config language, built-in treesitter and LSP. But some of neovim's limits come from decisions built into its core, and rewriting parts of it in faster C or Rust won't remove them. I tried working around them. In the end, fixing them meant starting again from a clean slate.

repositories.name: a-psychos-gd-tool
repositories.description: a node-based graphic design tool

paragraphs: Hosted version: a-psychos-gd-tool.vercel.app — needs a WebGPU browser (Chrome/Edge 113+ or Safari 18+).

A node-based graphic design tool that runs in the browser, on the GPU. You build a poster by wiring nodes on a canvas: text is shaped into vector outlines, vectors are warped and combined, rasters are blurred and dithered — every conversion is an explicit node on a typed wire, never a hidden coercion. The engine only re-computes what a change actually touches, so dragging a parameter stays interactive even in deep graphs.
Status: experimental, under active development. 35 node types; undo/redo is built in (⌘/Ctrl Z, ⇧⌘/Ctrl Z); persistence is not built yet (see Roadmap).

repositories.name: consculpta
repositories.description: Consculpta: breed 3D sculptures from formulas over simplex noise, raymarched in WebGL 2, with an optional AI co-breeder.

paragraphs: Interactive evolution of 3D sculptures from formulas over simplex noise, raymarched in WebGL 2.

Each sculpture is the region where a formula over 3D simplex noise rises above an iso level inside a sphere, cube or drum. Formulas are trees of noise, trigonometry and space transforms (twist, mirror, rotate, warp). Every offspring changes its parent's tree by tweaking a number, swapping a function, grafting a new branch, wrapping a node or cutting one out. About one offspring in twelve switches to strands: thin filaments traced where the formula's surface crosses a rotated copy of itself. The page evaluates each formula on 520 sample points to normalise it, estimate a safe raymarching step…
Simplex noise by Ian McEwan, Ashima Arts and Stefan Gustavson (MIT). Colours use Inigo Quilez's cosine palettes. Shader code exports a standalone Shadertoy shader with the formula compiled in.

paragraphs: TileDB Embedded is a high performant storage engine for dense and sparse multi-dimensional arrays. R6.tiledb is built on top of R6 object-oriented system and extends tiledb R package with base classes, which represent TileDB Arrays and Groups, as well as with subclasses that encapsulate additional methods. It provides also functional wrappers, convenient utilities and S3 methods.

The package can be helpful for developing domain specific applications or unified data architectures by extending the base classes. For day-to-day operations, the functional interface makes it easier to work with existing TileDB resources.

JSBT is a library and binary format for serializing real JavaScript object graphs – not just JSON‑like data. It is built around the needs of JS/TS runtimes and can safely serialize:
JSBT is ideal for Node ↔ Node, Node ↔ Browser, Browser ↔ Browser, worker/IPC channels, and any JS‑only distributed system where you care about structure, types and size, not just plain JSON.

Dates, BigInts, TypedArrays, Maps, Sets, Symbols
Class instances (with optional reconstruction of original prototypes)
Large, repetitive structured data with aggressive size deduplication
JSON cannot represent undefined, NaN, Infinity, -0, Map, Set, BigInt, circular references, or shared objects.

paragraphs: An online version of Romanian Whist, the trick-taking card game where you bid exactly how many tricks you'll take and lose points for every one you miss by. Three to six players share a table in real time, empty seats are filled by bots, and the server deals every card.
The practice table at /demo needs no account. You pick a table of 3 to 6, and bots fill the other seats. The whole game runs in the browser.
features: Real-time multiplayer rooms joined with a six-digit code, using Supabase Realtime
Bots that bid from an estimate of their hand and then play to make that bid, ducking tricks once they have enough
Seat recovery: if a player disconnects, a bot covers their seat after 15 seconds, and they take it back mid-round when they return
A contract tracker on each player's plate showing tricks bid, tricks taken and whether they've gone over
A side panel with standings and every player's bid and result for each round, so streaks are easy to follow

repositories.description: 一个轻量级的 Python Web 框架，一站式集成 MCP SSE、StreamHTTP 和 MCPO 协议，助你轻松构建MCP Server🔥

paragraphs: Pywss（发音 /piːwaɪz/，类似 pwhys）是一个轻量级的 Python Web 框架，它基于 Python3.6+ 特性构建。
与 Flask、Django 等主流框架不同的是，Pywss 的底层并没有实现 WSGI 接口协议。 其编程风格也更类似于 Gin、Iris 等框架，因此对于熟悉这些框架的开发者来说，Pywss 是一个非常值得探索的项目。
features: 简单：拒绝海量参数，减少心智负担。了解上下文 pywss.Context 即刻启程。
快速：引入线程池机制，减少并发场景下线程创建/销毁开销。
优雅：ctx.next 真的太优雅了。如果你也和我一样喜欢，那我觉得这件事情，泰裤辣！！
标准化：集成了部分 OpenAPI（Swagger）能力，方便开发者快速生成 API 文档并进行调试。
支持WebSocket：开箱即用的 WebSocket 能力。

whatItDoes.text: Pywss（发音 /piːwaɪz/，类似 pwhys）是一个轻量级的 Python Web 框架，它基于 Python3.6+ 特性构建。

repositories.name: tinytipy
repositories.description: Diff-driven text morphing with a live typing cursor and framework adapters

paragraphs: Diff-driven text morphing: animate only the changed parts when transforming text from A → B, with a typing cursor. Korean IME-aware.

Given two strings, tinytipy diffs them, then animates the transition — erasing the removed characters and typing the inserted ones (composing Korean syllable-by-syllable like a real IME), while shared text stays put. Perfect for showing speech-recognition corrections, AI edits, form fixes, or any A→B text reveal.

Because the diff marks shared substrings as equal, they render once and never change. The morph spends its time only on delete runs (erased char-by-char) and insert runs (typed frame-by-frame). The cursor anchors to whichever run is actively being edited.
features: 🎯 Only the diffs move — unchanged text is never re-typed.
⌨️ Korean IME composition — 최근 types as ㅊ → 최 → 최ㄱ → 최그 → 최근.
✨ Live trailing cursor — an overlay caret follows each edit without shifting text, then keeps blinking at the end.
🧩 One core, every framework — React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and vanilla DOM adapters. Import only what you use.
🪶 Tiny & tree-shakeable — framework-agnostic core, side-effect-free adapters, and an explicitly preserved stylesheet.

whatItDoes.text: Diff-driven text morphing: animate only the changed parts when transforming text from A → B, with a typing cursor. Korean IME-aware.

audience.text: Given two strings, tinytipy diffs them, then animates the transition — erasing the removed characters and typing the inserted ones (composing Korean syllable-by-syllable like a real IME), while shared text stays put. A seeded fake-data engine fills them in dependency order, so every foreign key points at a real row. The built-in REST simulator handles GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE with filtering operators, full-text search, multi-key sorting, pagination, field projection, relation expansion, nested routes, schema validation with 422 errors, simulated latency and a chaos…

Seeded, reproducible fake data generated in topological (FK-safe) order
REST simulator: CRUD, filters (gte/lte/ne/like), q search, multi-sort, page/limit, fields, expand, nested routes
Validation engine with 422 details (types, enums, ranges, emails, FK existence, uniqueness, unknown fields)
Latency simulation and chaos mode (random 500s) for resilience testing

A tesseract is essentially a 4D cube; what you see on the website is a visualization of the points of the tesseract undergoing two perspective projections): once from 4D into 3D, and again from 3D into 2D (which you see on your computer screen!)

The graphics were created with p5.js. I did not use the library's built-in WebGL 3D renderer. Rather, everything you see is represented by 2D shapes, the positions and scales of which I calculated manually (for whatever reason, doing something like this has been on my bucket list).

whatItDoes.text: I created this visualization as an extra credit project for the multivariable calculus class I took in the fall of my senior year of high school.

repositories.name: engine262
repositories.description: An implementation of ECMA-262 in JavaScript

paragraphs: While helping develop new features for JavaScript, I've found that one of the most useful methods of finding what works and what doesn't is being able to actually run code using the new feature. Babel is fantastic for this, but sometimes features just can't be nicely represented with it. Similarly, implementing a feature in one of the engines is a large undertaking, involving long compile times and annoying bugs with the optimizing compilers.

engine262 is a tool to allow JavaScript developers to have a playground where new features can be quickly prototyped and explored. As an example, adding do expressions to this engine is as simple as the following diff:

This simplicity applies to many other proposals, such as optional chaining, pattern matching, the pipeline operator, and more. This engine has also been used to find bugs in ECMA-262 and test262, the test suite for conforming JavaScript implementations.
features: 100% Spec Compliance
Ease of modification
Speed at the expense of any of the goals
Do not expose $ and $262 global variable for test262 test suite.
Do not start an inspector.

repositories.name: snowglobe
repositories.description: Package Docker into WASM

paragraphs: Package a Docker image into a website that runs it in the browser. snowglobe boots your image on real Linux inside armless, a 64-bit ARM machine compiled to WebAssembly, snapshots it once your app is ready, and writes a folder of static files. Visitors get your program running in their tab in about a second, with no server behind it.

This is an experiment. Everything runs on an emulated 64-bit ARM CPU (translated to WebAssembly as it runs), so expect it to be slower than native. A site can have up to 8 CPUs (--cpus), which helps programs that use them (the Elixir demo runs CPU-bound tasks about 4× faster on 4); the demos use 2, to stay light on phones.

paragraphs: Exemplary implementation of an offline capable, location based React app utilizing service-workers. Shows an app install banner on supported devices.
On a successful api call the location is backed up into local storage, if location data is unavailable, the backup from storage is used.

More Importantly: If the dynamic api call fails (Device is offline) the backed up location is used to repeat the call, thus receiving an already cached response. This enables a seamless online to offline experience. Ultimately displaying data from the last available location.
features: Service workers are generated using Google's sw-precache

paragraphs: "The farmer should not have to interpret technical sensor data. Setu interprets the environment and tells the farmer what is happening, why it matters, and what action is being taken."
Setu is an end-to-end, IoT-enabled environmental management and automation system purpose-built for silkworm rearing sheds worldwide.

Silkworms (Bombyx mori) are highly sensitive to microclimate variations. Even minor deviations in temperature and relative humidity across growth instars (Instars 1 through 5) can cause crop failure, disease outbreak (Flacherie, Grasserie), or inferior cocoon quality. Setu solves this by combining IoT sensing, real-time worldwide weather tracking, deterministic automation rules, hardware safety interlocks, and multilingual explainable AI recommendations in English, Kannada (ಕನ್ನಡ), and Telugu (తెలుగు).

repositories.name: HomRec
repositories.description: Screen recorder built for weak PCs.

paragraphs: A native C/C++ screen recorder for low-spec Windows machines. FFmpeg for encoding, no GPU requirement, no background services. Free and open source (GPLv3) - no activation, no license keys, no paid features.

HomRec targets a specific problem: general-purpose screen recorders (OBS, Bandicam) assume more CPU/GPU headroom than a lot of real-world machines have. HomRec is built to avoid that assumption entirely - no compositor, no GPU dependency, no background services beyond what active recording requires.

The application is 100% native C/C++: UI (wxWidgets), capture pipeline, audio, plugin host (Lua 5.4), and console all compile into hr.exe. At runtime it needs FFmpeg for encoding and the runtime .dll files that ship beside it (wxWidgets and the MinGW runtime); the installer and the portable archive include both. paragraphs: In this simple but comprehensive demo, Confluent Platform acts as true central nervous system, ingesting data from several edge devices. These devices send important information like temperature and GPS location, but they use many different communication and application protocols, such as MQTT, HTTP, Kafka, CoAP, Syslog, and RabbitMQ (just to name a few). This diversity reflects the IoT world's nature, where a single standard is more the exception than the norm, requiring a robust, highly scalable, and adaptable data streaming platform.

Confluent Platform stands out because it can take in data from all these different sources in real time, thanks to its wide range of connectors. Once the data arrives, it's transformed into a common format using ksqlDB, a tool for processing data streams. This makes the data easier to understand and use decoupling upstream applications. After processing, the data is sent to Elasticsearch, where it's displayed on a Kibana dashboard. This gives a clear view of the data in real time. The data is also saved in PostgresDB for later use. This demonstration underlines the Confluent Platform's…

A data fabric is an integrated architecture and set of data services that provide consistent capabilities across a choice of endpoints spanning on-premises and multiple cloud environments. It facilitates the seamless integration, management, and analysis of data across different platforms, systems, and environments, enabling organizations to access and share their data more efficiently. By automating data discovery, governance, and management, a data fabric helps organizations to break down data silos, improve collaboration, and drive more informed decision-making. This architecture is…
features: Kafka Ecosystem: Built on Apache Kafka, Confluent provides a high-throughput, scalable, and resilient messaging system that can handle the vast data flows typical in a data fabric architecture.
Real-time Data Processing: Confluent enables real-time data processing and analytics, allowing organizations to gain immediate insights and respond quickly to changing conditions.

Unified Data Integration: With a wide array of connectors and integrations, Confluent facilitates the unification of data from disparate sources and formats, crucial for the data fabric's goal of comprehensive data…
Schema Management: Confluent Schema Registry helps maintain consistent data formats and enforces compatibility rules, ensuring data integrity across the fabric.

Security and Governance: Confluent provides robust security features, including encryption, access control, and audit capabilities, essential for maintaining data privacy and compliance within a data fabric.

repositories.name: unmark-web
repositories.description: Independent browser-first client that strips invisible Unicode marks and C2PA/EXIF/XMP/ID3 metadata from text, images, audio and video locally, or via the watermarks-remover Python service (MIT)

paragraphs: Removes the digital watermarks and provenance marks that AI tools leave on what they generate: the invisible Unicode characters hidden in text, and the C2PA, EXIF, XMP and ID3 metadata carried inside image, audio and video files. It also tells you, honestly, which watermarks it cannot remove: statistical ones live in how tokens were sampled and pixel-domain ones live in the image itself, so no metadata strip touches them. The Inspector tab tests for those separately.
Independent, browser-first web client for guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover, inspired by and compatible with its HTTP API. Not affiliated with the upstream project.
Live demo: · Local: open index.html or run python3 servelocal.py.
features: Runs entirely in the browser for text (Layer A: invisible Unicode / homoglyph spaces), for PNG / JPEG / WebP / AVIF / HEIC / BMP / GIF / TIFF and MP4 / MOV / M4A / WAV / MP3 / FLAC metadata (C2PA, EXIF, XMP, text…
Optionally drives the upstream Python service (server.py) for everything else: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, ODT, EPUB, LaTeX, and pixel-domain backends.

The JavaScript engines are line-for-line ports of upstream's textunicode.py, imagemeta.py, avmeta.py, scorestylometry.py and detectgumbel.py, and a parity test suite asserts identical output (same characters…

A Watermark Inspector tab runs every detector on one input and reports each separately across the character, metadata and statistical layers, and can re-run them after a Layer A clean to show what the cleaner did not…

repositories.description: Cost-aware customer retention system for a fictional streaming platform — calibrated churn modeling, SHAP-based retention levers, ROI-optimized intervention policy, deployed decision-support tool.

paragraphs: Cost-aware customer-retention system for a fictional streaming subscription business (synthetic data with realistic churn bands, tenure spikes, engagement cohorts and an intervention menu). End-to-end: a calibrated churn model, a budget-constrained intervention policy, a randomized experiment, and a deployed decision-support tool. Sister project to StreamFlix-AB-Testing and StreamFlix-RAG-evaluation, built on the same StreamFlix context.

Bottom line (per month, full 2.1M base, $200k budget): the blanket $5-credit campaign loses $252k. The targeted policy earns +$174k net expected value at 1.87× ROI, a $426k monthly swing on $133k less spend. A randomized holdout confirms the $5 credit works on average (12.6% of would-be churners retained), but an uplift model trained on it ranks users no better than chance, so the propensity-based policy ships and the uplift model doesn't. Synthetic data with assumed lever uplifts; see Limitations. Recommendation in reports/decisionmemo.md.
Fastest way in: reports/PROJECTSUMMARY.md — one-page catalog of the three parts (churn model → decision rule → experiment and uplift test), with every headline number traced to its source notebook.

whatItDoes.text: Cost-aware customer-retention system for a fictional streaming subscription business (synthetic data with realistic churn bands, tenure spikes, engagement cohorts and an intervention menu). End-to-end: a calibrated churn model, a budget-constrained intervention policy, a randomized experiment, and a deployed decision-support tool. Sister project to StreamFlix-AB-Testing and StreamFlix-RAG-evaluation, built on the same StreamFlix context.

repositories.name: taxtriage
repositories.description: TaxTriage is a Nextflow workflow designed to agnostically identify and give confidences of microbial organisms within short- or long-read metagenomic NGS data. This flexible tool was developed with various use-cases of mNGS in mind.

paragraphs: TaxTriage is a metagenomic decision-support workflow—not simply a collection of QC, classification, and alignment tools. It converts short- or long-read metagenomic sequencing data into organism-level evidence, resolves ambiguous alignments among related references, ranks detections with the TASS confidence score, and packages the results in a self-contained, highly interactive HTML report.
Many metagenomic Nextflow workflows end with tool-specific files and a MultiQC summary. TaxTriage adds a post-alignment interpretation layer designed to help users answer harder questions:
TaxTriage is intended for research, surveillance, and early-stage outbreak investigation. It is not intended for use as a standalone diagnostic capability.
features: Is an organism supported by distributed, high-quality, reference-specific evidence rather than a small ambiguous pileup?
How should evidence be interpreted when reads align to several closely related organisms or strains?
Which detections remain credible after shared regions and competing references are considered?
How do detections vary across samples, specimens, time points, locations, hosts, diseases, and other supplied metadata?

repositories.name: zakat-eligibility-triage-n8n
repositories.description: AI triage for zakat-eligibility review: two model calls, deterministic refusal, human-only outcomes, operational layer on n8n. Live demo linked.

paragraphs: This fork moves the pipeline's operational half onto n8n. Three workflows in n8n/ decide when a campaign is read, what happens when a provider fails, and who hears about it. They decide nothing about what may be said about a campaign. The original — button-driven, no orchestrator — is at kianis4/zakat-eligibility-triage and runs untouched beside this one. The reasoning is ADR-0010.

A triage agent for crowdfunding campaigns. It reads a submitted campaign, assembles the evidence a zakat determination would turn on, names what the text leaves missing or contested, and hands the file to a qualified human reviewer. It never issues a religious ruling. Every claim it makes is traceable to a span of the campaign it read, and nothing it produces is a score.

paragraphs: Before an AI agent pays for an API, vet402 has already bought it with its own money and shows what came back, with the payment on chain.

On Solana, Tempo and Base since 2026-09-28 (UTC). The current counts (purchases, sellers, payments settled, answers that came back, and payments that settled with nothing usable back) are at the top of the site's first page and in site/rank.json: the groups[] entry with id main, its totals (the top-level totals include Algorand).

"Came back with an answer" means the payment settled and the seller answered 2xx with a non-empty body (for the Tempo census purchases, whose runner kept no body: 2xx; the Tempo re-purchases are tested for an empty body). On Solana, Tempo and Base the runner checked each payment on chain before calling it settled. vet402 did not check that the answer is what the listing promised; whether its keys matched what the seller declared is a separate column.

repositories.description: Pre-mortem risk map: find how your plan fails before it does. Drag risks onto a likelihood-and-damage grid, run 2,000 survival simulations, and explore a 3D universe. Built with plain JavaScript, Node and MongoDB.

paragraphs: Preflight is a pre-mortem tool. You imagine your plan has already failed, list every reason why, and drag each cause onto a map of how likely it is against how damaging it would be. It then runs 2,000 simulations of your plan and tells you the odds it survives.

The project has two separate parts: a static client (one HTML file) and a small server that stores plans in a database (MongoDB or SQLite). Behind the app sits a draggable 3D universe you can open and explore.
features: Risk map: drag glowing orbs across a likelihood and damage grid. Score, size and colour update live.
Plan danger score: one number from 0 to 100 with a gradient meter and a flight rank, from "Cleared for takeoff" to "Mayday".
Survival simulation: runs 2,000 trials and shows the chance your plan survives, with a histogram of calm and disaster runs.
Next best move: points at the highest-danger risk you have not handled yet.
Handled risks: mark a risk as handled and its danger drops by 70%.

repositories.name: search-esque
repositories.description: Elasticsearch-compatible query DSL and aggregations over SQLite

paragraphs: Elasticsearch-compatible query DSL and aggregations over SQLite.

Write the query you already know, bool, term, range, match, aggs with terms and datehistogram, and run it over a plain SQLite file. No search engine, no extension, no server. The same crate compiles to a native binary, to WebAssembly for the browser, and to a Python extension.

Why SQLite only: this is for light, local, throwaway data. The index is one file, facets are exact counts, and nothing you do here can hammer a shared database server with aggregation queries. A .db on a laptop, or in a browser tab, is the whole deployment.
features: term on a keyword field ignores letter case.
A quoted number for a number field is refused, not coerced.
Counts are exact, never approximate. terms has no shardsize.
should is supported only directly in a bool; minimumshouldmatch beyond 0 and 1 is refused.
With no sort, hits come back in id order.

whatItDoes.text: Elasticsearch-compatible query DSL and aggregations over SQLite.

repositories.name: petri_bloom
repositories.description: Framework for generating behavioral evaluations of frontier AI models.

paragraphs: Welcome to Petri Bloom, an implementation of the Bloom automated evaluation tool using the Petri auditor/target framework.

Bloom generates evaluation suites that probe LLMs for specific behaviors (sycophancy, self-preservation, political bias, etc.). Given a "seed" configuration describing the target behavior and evaluation parameters, Bloom produces diverse test scenarios, runs conversations with the target model, and scores the results. The evaluation suite grows differently depending on how it's seeded—unlike fixed benchmarks, Bloom evaluations should be cited with their full seed configuration for reproducibility.

whatItDoes.text: Welcome to Petri Bloom, an implementation of the Bloom automated evaluation tool using the Petri auditor/target framework.

paragraphs: A script I run on demand that answers one question about my scheduled Claude Code agents: what is each one allowed to touch? It reads the permission config they run under, reads each agent's instructions, and diffs both against a written acceptable-use policy.

Then a just-in-time pass asks the follow-up: for each agent, which standing permissions every run uses, and which could be granted per run and dropped. It answers from the transcripts the runs left behind, not from config.
This is the third of a set. skill-regression-harness asks whether the right agent fires. scheduled-agent-detector asks whether it did its job. This one asks what it's allowed to do.

paragraphs: A zero-config, fully reproducible presentation environment powered by Marp and Nix. 1. Write slides in Markdown 2. Build pixel-identical HTML, PDF, and cover images anywhere 3. Forget toolchain drift forever

Presentations have a tooling problem. Proprietary editors lock content into binary formats. Web slide builders die when their SaaS goes offline. Even "plain HTML" decks tend to drift the moment a teammate runs a different Node version, a different Chromium, or a different font fallback.
This repository is a deliberate, opinionated answer to that problem:
features: Markdown-first authoring: Slides are text. They diff cleanly, review like code, and survive any tool you'll ever use.
Marp for rendering: A mature, fast, themeable Markdown-to-slide engine with a real CLI, live server, and PDF export.

Nix flakes for the toolchain: The Marp CLI, the headless browser used for PDF rendering, the emoji set, and every supporting binary are pinned by hash. Anyone with Nix can reproduce your deck, byte-for-byte, five years…
Convention over configuration: Drop a .md file under slides/, get HTML, PDF, and a PNG cover. No project per deck, no boilerplate, no scripts to copy.

paragraphs: Fare Terminal is airfare market intelligence — think "stock ticker meets research terminal" for flight prices, not a booking site. For a set of tracked airport-pair routes, it turns repeated observed offers into a current benchmark price, price history, a fair-value range, detected market events (price drops, carrier moves, volatility spikes, ...), and a plain-language buy/wait recommendation.

Every claim the app makes is explicitly split into what was observed (a plain factual statement pulled directly from the data — "current benchmark is $403.00") versus what was inferred from it (an interpretation, always carrying its own confidence level — "consistent with a neutral signal, high confidence"). Recommendations expose their reasoning the same way: an "Observed" list, an "Inferred" list, and a "Counterevidence & limitations" list, so a decision never rests on an unexplained badge. repositories.name: nina-mir
repositories.description: about me

paragraphs: | browser-use/browser-use #5672 | Stopped two LLM provider adapters from authenticating third-party endpoints with the user's OpenAI key. ChatDeepSeek and ChatCerebras passed apikey=None into an AsyncOpenAI client pointed at api.deepseek.com and api.cerebras.ai, so the SDK fell back to OPENAIAPIKEY — sending it to a different vendor. The env vars the docs promised were never read. Audited all nine adapters to derive the discriminator (an OpenAI-SDK client at a non-OpenAI baseurl), which found exactly these two and cleared the rest; reported the negative results alongside the fix.

| | docling-project/docling #4457 | Found and fixed a bug nobody had reported: numbering inside a Word text box leaked onto the paragraph holding it. A floating text box is stored inside an anchor paragraph, but docling resolved list numbering with a descendant search (.//w:numPr) that reached into the box — so plain body text came out as a list item (issue #4456, which I filed). OOXML permits w:numPr only under w:pPr, so the search could only ever find another paragraph's numbering. Proved causality by diffing a full conversion with the lookup narrowed: exactly one line of the document…

| | python-visualization/folium 3 PRs | #2263 · Root-caused a bug open since 2021: GeoJSON tooltips came up empty on multi-geometry features. The feature never reached the child layers Leaflet wraps in a FeatureGroup (issue #1520). Fix verified against all eight geometry types plus nested GeometryCollections, with a Selenium regression test.
features: Filed adobe/react-spectrum #10411 with a live reproduction — the S2 docs playground was emitting Tooltip code samples that didn't typecheck; a maintainer shipped the fix the next day.
Posted browser-tested findings on react-spectrum #8027 and mdn/content #45005, including the negative results.

whatItDoes.text: | browser-use/browser-use #5672 | Stopped two LLM provider adapters from authenticating third-party endpoints with the user's OpenAI key. ChatDeepSeek and ChatCerebras passed apikey=None into an AsyncOpenAI client pointed at api.deepseek.com and api.cerebras.ai, so the SDK fell back to OPENAIAPIKEY — sending it to a different vendor. The env vars the docs promised were never read. Audited all nine adapters to derive the discriminator (an OpenAI-SDK client at a non-OpenAI baseurl), which found exactly these two and cleared the rest; reported the negative results alongside the fix.

paragraphs: 为世界古典美术中的人、动物与环境进行生态模拟 —— 画中的生物与植物都是自主智能体（Autonomous Agents）， 平台吸收当代最强的拟生（Artificial Life / Behavioral Animation）技术，让古画"活"过来。
首个场景：《竹虎溪涧图》（tiger.html）—— 以狩野山乐《竹虎图》中名为“斑阑”的猛虎为主角， 竹林与雪景溪涧的环境取自东京国立博物馆藏·雪舟《四季花鸟图》屏风的溪涧意趣。

第二幅：《寒梅归雁图》（plum.html）—— 五层纵深布景：前景山石与石径 → 繁花古梅及伴生小竹芦苇 → 塘边缓坡（塘水环绕梅根成湾、留出 1 米土地，栖雁立于坡）→ 静水塘与上空归飞雁群（V 字编队、盘旋渐降、 定翼进近 → 拉平扑翼减速 → 触水滑跑；踏水助跑起飞、巡航收蹼、空中翼面全展）→ 四重没骨远山（西湖式层峦，缓丘相叠、无孤峰）。 大雁为雁形目（ANSERIFORMES·鸭科·雁属）自主智能体，躯体由 AvianBodyBuilder 比例覆写生成（长颈/肥体/阔翼）。 该画配置独立成页：plum-config.html（与竹虎溪涧配置分开，归雁/花木/环境/机位/歌单全参数可调）。
